chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a thief who entered upon a woman to steal her belongings. When he had gathered the clothes, his desire overcame him, and he had intercourse with her. Then her son stirred, so he went to him and killed him with an axe that he had with him.
When he had finished, he carried the clothes and went to leave, but she attacked him with the axe and killed him. The next day, his family came demanding retaliation for his blood.

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "His associates who sought retaliation for his blood are liable for the blood money of the boy. The thief is liable, from what he left behind, for four thousand dirhams because he forced her regarding her private part, since he is a fornicator, and it is to be paid from his wealth. There is nothing against the woman for her killing him, because he was a thief."

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: the monetary compensation due from the thief’s estate
key_terms.دِيَةَ الْغُلَامِ: the blood money owed for the killed boy
key_terms.زَانٍ: one guilty of illicit sexual intercourse
key_terms.فَرْجِهَا: her private part, referring here to sexual violation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a thief assaults a woman, kills her child, and the woman then kills him?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning a thief who committed theft, sexual assault, and murder, and who was then killed by the assaulted woman. The Imam عليه السلام rules on liability for the slain child, the financial penalty due from the thief’s estate, and the absence of liability upon the woman for killing him in that circumstance.
